introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Statistics Paper 2 (0770/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

Le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question ni pour l'épreuve ; les points par partie sont recopiés tels qu'imprimés (leur somme est 105) et `points` de chaque exercice est laissé vide.
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : tous les corrigés sont rédigés et chaque valeur numérique a été recalculée par script (sympy).

Scan de 3 pages (page de garde + 2 pages de questions) : les questions 1 à 10 sont complètes et se suivent, aucune page ne semble manquer. L'étiquette imprimée en haut à gauche de la page de garde dit « Pure Maths With Mechs 2 » alors que le cadre « Subject Title » dit « Pure Mathematics With Statistics », code 0770, et que le pied de page porte 2022/0770/2 : le cadre et le code 0770 ont été retenus (Statistics).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $z$ and $w$ are two complex numbers, solve the simultaneous equations
$$3z + w = 9 + 11i, \qquad iw - z = -8 - 2i,$$
giving the answers in the form $a + bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are real constants. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the first equation, $w = 9 + 11i - 3z$. Substitute into the second:
$$i(9 + 11i - 3z) - z = -8 - 2i \;\Rightarrow\; 9i - 11 - 3iz - z = -8 - 2i.$$
Collect the terms in $z$:
$$-(1 + 3i)z = -8 - 2i - 9i + 11 = 3 - 11i \;\Rightarrow\; z = \frac{-3 + 11i}{1 + 3i}.$$
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1 - 3i$:
$$z = \frac{(-3 + 11i)(1 - 3i)}{(1 + 3i)(1 - 3i)} = \frac{-3 + 9i + 11i - 33i^2}{10} = \frac{30 + 20i}{10} = 3 + 2i.$$
Then $w = 9 + 11i - 3(3 + 2i) = 9 + 11i - 9 - 6i = 5i$.

Check in the second equation: $iw - z = i(5i) - (3 + 2i) = -5 - 3 - 2i = -8 - 2i$. And $3z + w = 9 + 6i + 5i = 9 + 11i$.
$$\boxed{z = 3 + 2i, \quad w = 0 + 5i}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of natural numbers. A relation $R$ is defined on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ by
$$(a, b)\,R\,(c, d) \iff \frac db = \frac ca.$$
Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Here $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$ (the definition divides by $a$ and $b$, so $0$ is excluded). All elements are therefore non-zero and divisions are legitimate. Note that $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d) \iff \dfrac db = \dfrac ca \iff ad = bc$.

An equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

**Reflexive.** For any $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$: $\dfrac{b}{b} = 1 = \dfrac{a}{a}$, so $(a, b)\,R\,(a, b)$.

**Symmetric.** Suppose $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d)$, i.e. $\dfrac db = \dfrac ca$, equivalently $ad = bc$. Then $cb = da$ (the same equation read the other way), that is $\dfrac{b}{d} = \dfrac{a}{c}$, which is exactly the condition for $(c, d)\,R\,(a, b)$.

**Transitive.** Suppose $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d)$ and $(c, d)\,R\,(e, f)$, i.e.
$$\frac db = \frac ca \quad\text{and}\quad \frac fd = \frac ec.$$
Multiply the two equalities:
$$\frac db \cdot \frac fd = \frac ca \cdot \frac ec \;\Rightarrow\; \frac fb = \frac ea \quad(\text{cancelling } d \ne 0 \text{ and } c \ne 0),$$
which says $(a, b)\,R\,(e, f)$.

$R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation. $\blacksquare$ (Its equivalence classes are the sets of pairs with the same ratio $\frac ab$.)
